result.topic_en: Formulas for the projection ellipse of an orbit (semi-axes, centre coordinates, inclination of the axis to the equinoctial line) using auxiliary angles, with a worked numerical example for the asteroid Juno using its 1810 elements.
result.transcription:
79.

Dadurch wird

$\alpha\cos(\mathcal{E}+\varepsilon) - \alpha e\cos\varepsilon = \varrho\cos(\lambda - \gamma - \Omega)$
$\mathfrak{b}\sin(\mathcal{E}+\varepsilon) - \mathfrak{b}e\sin\varepsilon = \varrho\sin(\lambda - \gamma - \Omega)$

Hier sind $\alpha$, $\mathfrak{b}$ die beiden halben Hauptaxen der Projectionsellipse
$-\alpha e\cos\varepsilon$, $-\mathfrak{b}e\sin\varepsilon$ die Coordinaten des Mittelpunkts, die Axe $2\alpha$ als
Abscissenlinie angenommen, $\gamma+\Omega$ deren Neigung gegen die Aequinoctiallinie.

Bei der Berechnung kann man noch folgende Hülfsgrössen einführen

$\cos [-k-] {+i+} = \tang k$, $\cos\varphi = \tang l$, $\frac{a}{\cos k\cos l} = c$, alsdann ist

$a(1-\cos\varphi\cos i) = c.\cos(k+l)$
$a(\cos i - \cos\varphi) = c.\sin(k-l)$
$a(1+\cos\varphi\cos i) = c.\cos(k-l)$
$a(\cos i + \cos\varphi) = c.\sin(k+l)$

methods.what: Parametrization of the projected orbit (projection ellipse) in terms of semi-axes, centre offset and angle relative to the equinoctial line
Auxiliary angles k, l and quantity c introduced to make the computation logarithm-friendly
Product-form identities expressing combinations of cos φ and cos i via the auxiliary angles
